evidence: Our experiments are mainly conducted on ImageNet-1K [4] benchmark.
The networks are optimized using stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with a momentum of 0.9 and a mini-batch of 160.
we also make experiments on CIFAR-100 benchmark [18], which contains 60K color images of 32x32 pixels
the inference time (ms) per image are 2.52 vs 2.68/2.84 (vanilla ResNet-50 vs GSoP-Net1/GSoP-Net2)
unresolved: No seed count, repetition count, or run-to-run variability is stated anywhere; all reported top-1/top-5 error, params, GFLOPs, and inference-time figures appear to be single-run point estimates (standard for CVPR 2019 ImageNet-scale training papers), so n_seeds and reports_variability='none' are inferred from absence, not an explicit statement.

n_models=3 counts the paper's own architecture variants (GSoP-Net1, GSoP-Net2, vanilla/baseline ResNet backbone); ablation configurations (covariance size, fusion scheme, per-stage block placement) are treated as sub-experiments on these architectures, not separate models -- a different counting convention could yield a higher number.

n_baselines=12 merges the competing methods listed across Table 5 (ImageNet-1K: He et al./ResNet, FBN, SORT, MPN-COV, iSQRT-COV, SE-Net, GENet, CBAM, ResNeXt, DropBlock, DRN-A-50) and Table 6 (CIFAR-100: adds CMPE, reuses He et al., SE-Net, MPN-COV) into one distinct-method count; exact de-duplication across the two tables involved judgment.

control_arm is not applicable in the backdoor/attack sense this schema is designed for -- this is a vision architecture paper with no attack/poisoning control arm, so left null rather than guessing a mapping onto 'vanilla network' baseline.
